headline: Google Gemini expands third-party app integrations with Airtable, Linear, Adobe, and more
summary: Google's AI assistant now connects directly with more services like Airtable, Linear, and Adobe. This enhances Gemini's utility for daily workflows, allowing users to pull information and manage tasks more efficiently.
details: Google is expanding Gemini's third-party app integrations, adding services like Airtable, Linear, Wispr AI, and Adobe. This move aims to make the AI assistant more useful for daily work and integrate it seamlessly into user workflows.
Users can now connect these apps to Gemini to directly pull relevant information. For instance, you can ask Gemini to retrieve meeting notes from Wispr Flow or pending tasks from Airtable databases.

These new integrations can be found in Gemini's settings under "Connected Apps" or summoned directly in a chat using the "@" symbol. This follows earlier additions, including Granola, Otter.ai, and Ticketmaster.

While these app-by-app additions improve Gemini's functionality, the article notes that this approach is slow compared to wider Model Context Protocol (MCP) support. Both Claude and ChatGPT utilize MCP for broader third-party integrations.

Currently, custom MCP apps for Gemini are limited to eligible personal accounts in the US, despite Gemini Spark supporting custom MCP endpoints. Broader MCP access would allow users to integrate many more apps and services at once, addressing Gemini's current limitations.
caption:
Google Gemini just got a major upgrade for your workflow! It now integrates directly with Airtable, Linear, Adobe, and more.

Google is expanding Gemini's third-party app integrations, adding services like Airtable, Linear, Wispr AI, and Adobe. This move aims to make the AI assistant more useful for daily work and integrate it seamlessly into user workflows.

Users can now connect these apps to Gemini to directly pull relevant information. For instance, you can ask Gemini to retrieve meeting notes from Wispr Flow or pending tasks from Airtable databases.

These new integrations can be found in Gemini's settings under "Connected Apps" or summoned directly in a chat using the "@" symbol. This follows earlier additions, including Granola, Otter.ai, and Ticketmaster.

While these app-by-app additions improve Gemini's functionality, the article notes that this approach is slow compared to wider Model Context Protocol (MCP) support. Both Claude and ChatGPT utilize MCP for broader third-party integrations.

Currently, custom MCP apps for Gemini are limited to eligible personal accounts in the US, despite Gemini Spark supporting custom MCP endpoints. Broader MCP access would allow users to integrate many more apps and services at once, addressing Gemini's current limitations.
